# Vendor Models and Semantic Modelling Products
Vendor stewardship, public access, licensing and regulatory status are different questions. Inclusion is discovery, not endorsement or a claim of failure.

| Entry | Category | Main review boundary |
|---|---|---|
| [Microsoft CDM](microsoft-cdm.md) | Common data model | Public content/code licences; schema and SDK dependencies |
| [Salesforce Financial Services](salesforce-financial-services.md) | Industry application models | Product, package and object representation |
| [IBM Industry Models](ibm-industry-models.md) | Industry model family | Offering, rights, tool and support lifecycle |
| [SAP One Domain Model](sap-one-domain-model.md) | Business domain model | Partial source retrieval; supported application integration |
| [Google Looker / LookML](google-looker-lookml.md) | Semantic modelling language | Language/product versus an actual authored model |

All five profiles are drafts. Implementation outcomes are not evaluated. A documented maintenance notice is linked from Microsoft CDM; it is not a customer failure report.

## How to assess a vendor model
- Identify the specific asset, owner, version and intended business use.
- Separate document access, asset reuse rights and runtime entitlement.
- Record product/tool dependencies and any evidence of portability.
- Capture local extensions, upgrade work and semantic exceptions.
- Keep vendor claims separate from measured customer outcomes.
- Assess regulatory mandate separately for the jurisdiction and use case.

Use [the catalogue classification guide](../../docs/catalogue-classification.md) and [the evidence policy](../../docs/evidence-policy.md). The same evidence rules apply to vendor, community and consortium assets.
